svg.text: Common Beginner Mistakes -- and Where Each Was Already Solved
74-89% of retail accounts lose (ESMA, Ch1 L6). The losses cluster around a short, fixable list.
The mistake
The fix (and the lesson that gives it)
No plan, trading on emotion
entering because it "looks ready"
Write a plan (L2); pre-commit the exit before entry (L1)
Risking too much per trade
one bad run ends the account
Fixed 1-2%, position-sizing formula (Ch3 L1); low effective leverage (Ch3 L2)
No stop, or moving the stop
widening it to avoid being closed
Stop at invalidation, set as an order, never widened (Ch1 L7, Ch3 L3)
Cutting winners, riding losers
the disposition effect (Ch4 L1)
Risk-to-reward minimum before entry; let OCO orders execute (Ch3 L3, Ch4 L1)
Overtrading / revenge trading
trading bored, confident, or to get even
Trade only rule-met setups; cap trades or enforce a cool-down (Ch4 L1)
Chasing news
no evidence for how a release behaves
Check the calendar; sit out events you have not studied (Ch2 L4)
Indicator overload / timeframe-shopping
tools until they agree; charts until one agrees
A few tools you understand; fixed top-down timeframes (Ch2 L1, L5)
Trusting unverified claims
signal groups, tips, guaranteed returns
Verify claims; a guaranteed-return promise is the clearest scam sign there is
Pre-trade checklist (catches them before)
Planned setup? Stop at invalidation, as an order?
Ratio clears minimum? Size within risk %? Not chasing?
Any "no" = no trade.
Trading journal (catches them after)
Every trade: setup, stop, target, size, R result,
and whether you followed the plan.
Measures real expectancy; reveals repeated mistakes.
Nearly every mistake is one thing: acting on feeling or hope instead of a pre-decided, evidence-checked rule.
